notes:
- **Your agent is on your phone.** Pair one from Settings and the same conversation is there: type
  to it, speak to it, hand it a file, and hear it answer out loud. What you type at your desk turns
  up on the phone too, and a message sent from the phone says it came from the phone.
- **The phone runs your agent, not just talks to it.** Rename it, change its face, switch a skill
  off, build a new one by hand, change how much thinking each reply gets, and read the Work board.
  Anything it has drafted and is waiting on you for shows up there to read.
- **A Now tab, above Chat, and the agent opens on it.** One screen for what needs you today: drafts
  waiting on a press, replies you are owed, reminders coming up, and what your agent is doing this
  minute. A draft whose moment has passed drops off it instead of sitting there.
- **A Calendar.** Your week in time order, putting together the calendar you connected, the
  reminders you set and the routines that are due, with a mark saying which is which. Until now the
  connected calendar was never drawn anywhere in the app.
- **Your to-do list has a place of its own.** It was in the Records table alongside people and
  orders, three presses in and with nothing on it saying what it was. It is a tab now, open tasks
  first, in the order they are due.
- **Ask your agent to switch AI and it switches.** "Use ChatGPT instead", "think harder from now
  on", "keep your answers cheap". If there is no key saved for the company you asked for, it tells
  you where to paste one instead of just saying no.
- **Running out of AI credit now says what to do about it.** The message names your provider's own
  billing page, the Start button says the same thing instead of printing the provider's error back
  at you, and the AI account card keeps that link where the key lives.
- **Rooms: several of your agents in one conversation.** Name one and it answers, the rest stay
  quiet. New room is in the agent list, under your agents.
- **Scheduled runs and the inbox watch cost about half what they did.** Work nobody is sitting
  waiting on goes out on the cheaper lane, and a second message in the same chat reads what the AI
  company already had rather than paying to send it all again.
- **Outlook works the way Gmail does.** A first look reads the mailbox and tells you what is in it,
  and your agent can file a mail into a folder you named on any of the three providers.
- **Getting started is one screen with things to press on it.** Three asks to choose from instead
  of five counts to read, the name and the face on one card, and your agent arrives wearing Ember's
  face and named for it. The walk around the page waits until the interview is over rather than
  talking across it.
- **A skill that arrives needing something walks you through it** instead of sitting there doing
  nothing, and Build a skill is a place you go under Skills, with a conversation of its own.
- **Your agent shows everything a turn did**, not only its last step. A turn that is taking a while
  says what it is doing at 45 seconds, 2, 4 and 6 minutes, and how to call it off. It stops on its
  own at eight.
- **The draft you had before an edit is one press away**, and saying "edit" opens the same editor
  that pressing Edit does.
- **New in the store:** Lead Desk, Writing Desk, Ready to Post, Common Questions, a Stripe digest,
  Job Hunt and Application Sweep.
- Ask for the same reminder a third time and your agent offers to make it a standing one rather
  than setting another copy.
- The app says Beta on the screens that carry the wordmark, because that is what it is.
- Fixed: a numbered list from your agent came out as 1, 1, 1.
- Fixed: the card asking one thing of you took 25 seconds to turn up after your first answer.
- Fixed: an icon and its word on a button could end up on separate lines.
